answer: A claimant may hold only one hay strip on the communal salt meadow that drains through a registered inlet. Cutting is allowed only after an ebb tide has firmed the ground, and the hay must be bound under a press block carved for that strip alone. Peers later reopen the same strip and accept the stack only if the press mark and moisture log match the cut record. A new strip has no accepted mark until one stack has dried, and the strip and block cannot be shared. An alias therefore needs a second strip, a second block, and a dry-down no one else can perform.
